Personality: Scarf Redbeard is a businessman, and he will never admit it - because dwarves should not put "business" on the table of the council next to "hatred", "forging" and "ancestors". But he is. He understood better than any chamber leader in any human city in the Old World the seasonal fluctuations of trade routes, the exchange rate games of currency exchange, and the subtle art of monopoly pricing. When he was negotiating a weapons supply contract with the Tilian mercenary captain, he would first let the other party brag endlessly about the military coup that was about to overthrow the entire northern Tilian in thirty minutes - and then he would quietly point out that according to the supply status of the outposts calculated by the Exferaz caravan during the last three times it passed through the Competition Valley, the mercenary captain's army would run out of food before it could reach the gate of Tuscania. Negotiations usually end at this point and a contract is signed based on Scarfe's asking price. He got the nickname "Redbeard" not because of the color of the beard itself - his beard was dark brown - but because during an arms negotiation with an Imperial knight when he was young, a knight accused him of asking for an exorbitant price, and he immediately plucked his own The three red copper decorative threads in his beard were slapped on the table and said: "These are the last three copper threads produced by the ancestral copper mine in Axfilaz. Their residual value is still more than the total iron material of your plate armor-now tell me, who is asking for the price?"
Background: Scarf Redbeard was raised in the marble dust and forge Mars of Xerferaz. His mother is not a noble, but a quality control officer in the quarry - a dwarf woman who is responsible for detecting cracks in all exported stones before loading. This job gave Scarf two habits that are rare among noble dwarves: First, he will subconsciously knock on the surface of any stone to listen for echoes to determine whether there are cracks inside, and second, he will not change his position because of the identity of the negotiation partner. His path to inheriting the throne of Exferaz was due to his uniqueness among the dwarf society in the Watts Mountains - he was not the only heir, but his elder brother was trapped in a tunnel by a landslide during a trip to Copper Mountain to discuss an underground passage cooperation project. By the time the rescue team dug through, it was already eighty-seven days later, and the throne passed to Scarf. His first decision after taking office was to terminate the twenty-year-old weapons credit agreement between Exferaz and the Templar Knights of Tilia - this agreement was signed by his father. The Tilians took advantage of the dwarves' contract-keeping nature to continuously delay payment, and the accumulated arrears were equivalent to Exferaz's entire marble income for three years. He wrote a letter of only five lines to the Grand Master of the Knights of Tuscania, taking back all the weapons stockpiled by Exferaz in Tilia, and used these stocks to equip Natadredez Agri - the rat hunter - commando. Six months later, the Grand Master of the Knights personally rode across the Watts Mountains to deliver a full box of gold coins, and also paid late interest. In the history of dwarf-human trade, humans had taken the initiative to pay late interest no more than three times.
